title: Duo acceptance: Duo Decks, the deck viewer (P3)
intro: Duo Decks' viewer, end to end: a Markdown deck opens beside its slides, the slides redraw as you type, templates are picked with ⌃⌘N or a chip, problems and exports live in the deck's bar, comments pin to slides, and a plain PowerPoint can become templates or a Duo deck. Everything here was approved on the [Duo Decks canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/Sk28K1tkHgwk6gHs7RFGqQ) (boards 9A and 10 to 13) and split view's [split-deck screen](https://github.com/dudgeon/duo-v2/blob/main/docs/design/split-view-handoff/screens/split-deck.html). The sample deck, its Northwind pack and the plain pptx are synthetic, in the checkout project.
setup: A window about 1440 wide, so the deck's split has room for both sides.

groupNotes.In checkout: a Duo deck beside its slide: The checkout project with decks/field-trial-review.md and its pack in templates/decks/northwind (the fixtures). The first card opens the deck; the rest of the group carries on from it.
groupNotes.In checkout: problems, export and commen: Carries on from the deck left open above.
groupNotes.The command line: duo2 against the acceptance Duo, with the deck open.

features.group: In checkout: a Duo deck beside its slides
features.title: A deck opens beside its slides
features.what: A Markdown file with `type: deck` opens as one split tab: its source on the left, its slides on the right, drawn from the deck exported in memory (DL-269).
steps: Open `decks/field-trial-review.md` in `checkout`.
features.expect: One tab reads `field-trial-review.md ⫼ Slides`. The left side is the Markdown; the right side is the deck's slides at the side's width with the deck bar on top (‹ › n/N, Select Shape, Export ⌄). The slides look like the Northwind pack (teal and orange, the logo and footer). If the window is narrow the split folds to one side with a rail at the far right; click it to unfold.
features.workMacWhy: Needs a deck and a template pack in a project; copy the fixture's decks/ and templates/decks/ folders

features.group: In checkout: a Duo deck beside its slides
features.title: The slides redraw as you type, and follow the caret
features.what: Edit the source and the slides redraw about a quarter of a second after you stop, without saving or flashing. The caret's slide becomes the current one, and a 2 pt mark in the left margin shows which lines belong to it.
steps: In slide 3 (Unattended rows) change `86%` to `88%`, and stop typing.
Click into slide 6's lines, then slide 2's.
features.expect: Slide 3 shows 88% without a save and keeps its scroll position. As the caret moves, the slides scroll to the caret's slide and the bar's count follows; a thin grey bar in the source's left margin spans the current slide's lines. Nothing is written to disk until you save.

features.group: In checkout: a Duo deck beside its slides
features.title: Slide chips instead of markup, and changing a slide's template
features.what: Each `<!-- slide: … -->` line shows as a chip, "Slide n · template ⌄". Clicking it lists the pack's templates; choosing one changes the slide's template, carrying content over by Duo's rules and moving what doesn't fit to the slide's speaker notes (DL-285, DL-281, DL-296).
steps: Look at the source: no `<!-- slide: … -->` text.
Click slide 2's chip (`bullets`) and choose `two-column`.
features.expect: Chips read "Slide 2 · bullets ⌄" and so on, with a thin rule above. After the change slide 2 is two-column with empty columns; its four points are in its speaker notes under "Not placed after changing to two-column: body", and a card under the slide says the points moved, with Move to left, Move to right, Split with Claude and Undo Change. One ⌘Z undoes the change. The file on disk still holds the comment markers (Obsidian and GitHub hide them too).

features.group: In checkout: a Duo deck beside its slides
features.title: ⌃⌘N adds a slide from a template
features.what: ⌃⌘N (Format › New Slide, only in a deck) adds a chip under the caret's slide with the pack's templates listed; typing filters; Return inserts the template's skeleton (DL-295).
steps: Put the caret in slide 3.
Press ⌃⌘N, type `k`, press Return.
Type a title.
features.expect: A list at the caret shows each template with a small picture, its name and its purpose; `k` leaves kpi. Return inserts a kpi slide after slide 3: a title line with the caret in it and headings value, label, context. The new slide appears on the right as you type. The pictures in the list are stand-ins drawn from each template's slots, not real slide thumbnails yet (Q-415). New Slide… isn't in the editor's right-click menu (Q-416).

features.group: In checkout: problems, export and comments
features.title: Problems in the deck's bar and under the slide
features.what: When the deck breaks its templates, the bar shows Problems ⌄ and the slide gets a card saying what and offering a fix (DL-304, DL-298).
steps: In slide 3 change the value to `86 percent of rows`.
Open Problems ⌄ and choose the problem.
Change the first slide's chip to an unknown name by editing the file in another editor, or type a slide marker by hand with `kip`, if you want to see a one-answer fix.
features.expect: "⚠ 1 problem ⌄" appears after the slide count; its menu lists the problem and choosing it shows slide 3 and the source line. Under slide 3 a card says the value is too long for kpi, with Go to Line and Send to Claude. An unknown template with one near match offers "Use kpi". The menus are drawn in the page and don't take arrow keys yet (C-144).

features.group: In checkout: problems, export and comments
features.title: Export ⌄: a dated PowerPoint, and the export state
features.what: Export ⌄ writes `<deck> YYYY-MM-DD HHmm.pptx` beside the deck, replacing the previous export (DL-282, DL-286); the bar says whether the export is current.
steps: Undo the long value from the last card.
Export ⌄ › Export as PowerPoint….
Edit a word in the deck.
Export ⌄ › Export Again, then Show Export in Finder.
features.expect: A notice says "Exported field-trial-review 2026-11-… .pptx · 9 slides" with Show in Finder and Open With ⌄. The bar then reads "Exported now" (or a few minutes ago); after your edit it reads "Changed since export". Export Again names the file it replaces and leaves only the newest one in decks/. Upload to Google Slides… is dimmed (later, ENH-307). Opening the exported file shows the same slides in the PowerPoint viewer.
features.workMacWhy: Any deck in a project; writes a pptx beside it

features.group: In checkout: problems, export and comments
features.title: Comment on a slide, and see the pin
features.what: Select Shape, pick a slot, Add Comment: the comment is written into the Markdown on its own line in that slot (Review in Markdown's convention), and a pin appears at the slot's corner; clicking the pin opens the thread in the source's margin (DL-284, DL-302).
steps: Select Shape, click slide 3's big number.
In the bar at the foot, press Add Comment and write `Rounded from 87.6?`.
Click the pin that appears on slide 3.
features.expect: The foot bar reads "value on slide 3 · '86%'" with Add Comment first. The margin composer opens on the value's lines without taking the keyboard from the slides; posting writes a signed comment line into the value slot. A small capsule with a speech mark and 1 appears at the value's top right; clicking it opens the thread in the source's margin. The comment never appears on the slide or in an export.

features.group: In checkout: starting from a PowerPoint
features.title: Make Templates… on a PowerPoint
features.what: On a plain pptx the bar's Make Templates… turns the slides into a grid with tick boxes; Make Templates with Claude pastes the pick and the inventory line into Claude's prompt without Return (DL-291).
steps: Open `docs/grower-update.pptx`.
Press Make Templates…, tick slides 3 and 7.
Press Make Templates with Claude (a Claude session in checkout, or Send To).
features.expect: The slides lie in a grid (two columns in a narrow pane, three when wider) with tick boxes; Make Templates… shows pressed. The foot bar reads "2 slides picked" with Cancel, Add to Pack ⌄ and Make Templates with Claude. Claude's prompt gets the request and `duo2 deck template inventory … --slides 3,7`, not sent. Leaving the mode returns to the same slide.

features.group: In checkout: starting from a PowerPoint
features.title: Convert to Duo Deck…
features.what: Convert to Duo Deck… opens a Duo sheet (pack, Into); Convert with Claude hands the conversion to the session with the `duo2 deck import` line (DL-294, DL-305).
steps: With `docs/grower-update.pptx` open, press Convert to Duo Deck….
Press Convert with Claude.
features.expect: A sheet hangs from the toolbar: "Convert grower-update.pptx to a Duo deck", Template pack northwind · this project, Into decks/grower-update.md, Cancel and Convert with Claude. Convert pastes the request and the import line into Claude's prompt without Return; the plan, Claude's questions about merging look-alike layouts and the report happen in the session. The pptx isn't changed.

features.group: In checkout: starting from a PowerPoint
features.title: File › New › New Deck…
features.what: New Deck… (File › New and Files' + menu) opens a sheet with a name, a folder, the template pack and what to start with; Create writes the deck and opens it in its split tab (DL-297, DL-305).
steps: File › New › New Deck….
Name it `autumn-trial`, keep northwind and A title slide, press Create.
features.expect: The sheet lists northwind (this project, 8 templates) above Duo Plain (built in), with a strip of template tiles. Create makes `decks/autumn-trial.md` with one title slide and opens it beside its slide. The tiles are wireframes until real thumbnails exist (Q-415). No shortcut.
features.workMacWhy: Uses the built-in pack if a project has none

features.title: duo2 deck: the slide on screen, going to a slide, problems and comments
features.what: `duo2 deck`, `deck go`, `deck pick`, `deck problems`, `deck comments` and `deck comment` let Claude see and move the deck viewer and comment on slides (DL-71).
steps: With the deck open, run `duo2 deck`, then `duo2 deck go 4`.
Run `duo2 deck problems`, `duo2 deck comments`.
Run `duo2 deck comment 2 "Too many words"`.
features.expect: `duo2 deck` names the deck, the slide on screen and the lines the caret is in; `deck go 4` moves both sides to slide 4. `deck problems` lists errors and notices with lines; `deck comments` lists threads by slide and slot. `deck comment` writes a signed comment under slide 2's marker and a pin appears on slide 2.
features.workMacWhy: duo2 ships in the app; reads, plus one comment in his own deck
